success_patterns: Pointers to media the agent cannot see or hear ('Seen here is...', 'instrument heard here') were ignored. The agent answered from the remaining textual descriptors and the entity the passages tie to them (The Incredibles, tambourine).

Where a clue was reproduced in a passage, the agent took the entity from that passage or from the passages that repeat the clue's distinctive phrase: 'I Can't Explain' demo -> Jimmy Page, the lyric line -> 'Losing My Religion', the lonely woodcarver -> Geppetto, Tynwald -> Isle of Man.

For clues about a person through a relative or work ('his grandfather, the adding machine inventor, ... Naked Lunch'), the agent answered the person the clue is about (the grandson/author), not the relative named in the descriptor.

A J! Archive game-board page showed the clue but no answer (Howard Hughes). The agent still treated the clue match as confirmation and filled the answer from the other passages whose facts matched (1976, plane, Houston).
For a lyric or quotation clue with 'this song / hit that contains the lines', the agent answered with the song title, found in passages where the lyric sits next to the title.

patch.reasoning: These successes reinforce behaviours that the skill covers only partly: ignoring 'seen here / heard here' media pointers, answering the subject of a relative-based descriptor, completing a clue match when the archive page gives no answer, and resolving lyric clues to the song title. Short, targeted additions avoid the over-long edits that were rejected in earlier steps.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content: - Pointers to unseen media ('Seen here is ...', 'this instrument heard here', 'shown here') are not part of the fact. Ignore them and answer from the remaining textual descriptors plus the entity the passages tie to them ('sock puppet version of this film, hidden on the DVD' -> The Incredibles; 'handheld percussion instrument a minstrel could use' -> tambourine). Never reply that the image or audio is missing.

edits.target: Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content:
- A game-board or recap page (e.g. 'JEOPARDY! Game - <date>') may repeat the clue with no answer. Treat it as confirmation that the clue is genuine. Take the answer from the other passages that match the clue's specific facts (year, place, event), plus your own knowledge ('dying on a plane en route to a Houston hospital in 1976' -> Howard Hughes).
- Lyric clues ('1991 hit that contains the lines "..."') want the song title. Look for passages where the lyric line sits next to a title, and give the bare title without quotation marks.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - Relative-based descriptors ('his grandfather, the adding machine inventor, ...', 'her sister, the actress ...') describe a relative. The answer is the person the clue is about (the 'he' or 'she' in the sentence, here the author of "Naked Lunch"), not the relative. Pick the name that the passages tie to ALL the clue's details.
